# Overview

This is a React-based visual pipeline builder application that allows users to create and manipulate node-based workflows through a drag-and-drop interface. The application uses ReactFlow to provide an interactive canvas where users can add various types of nodes (Input, Output, LLM, Text, and several specialized nodes), connect them together, and build complex data processing pipelines. The project is bootstrapped with Create React App and runs on port 5000 with configuration for Replit hosting.

# User Preferences

Preferred communication style: Simple, everyday language.

# System Architecture

## Frontend Architecture

**Problem**: Need to build an interactive, visual pipeline editor with drag-and-drop functionality
**Solution**: React-based single-page application using ReactFlow library
**Rationale**: ReactFlow provides out-of-the-box node-graph capabilities, while React enables component-based architecture for different node types

### Component Structure

The application follows a modular component architecture:

- **App Component**: Main orchestrator that composes the toolbar, canvas UI, and submit button
- **PipelineToolbar**: Houses draggable node templates that users can drag onto the canvas
- **PipelineUI**: The main ReactFlow canvas where nodes are placed and connected
- **Node Components**: Individual node types with specific handles and fields
  - **Core Nodes**: Input, Output, LLM, Text (original nodes)
  - **Extended Nodes**: Calculator, Filter, Delay, Transformer, Router (showcase nodes)
- **BaseNode**: Factory pattern implementation for creating consistent node components with shared behavior

**Design Pattern**: The BaseNode uses a factory/configuration pattern where nodes are created by passing configuration objects rather than writing boilerplate code for each node type. This promotes code reuse and consistency. The abstraction supports:
- Function-based default values for dynamic field initialization (e.g., id-derived naming)
- Flexible handle positioning (top, bottom, left, right) with custom styling
- Multiple field types (text, number, select, textarea)
- Custom node styling (backgrounds, borders, colors)
- Minimal code per node (typically 10-30 lines vs 40+ lines without abstraction)

### State Management

**Problem**: Need to manage global state for nodes, edges, and user interactions across components
**Solution**: Zustand state management library with a centralized store
**Rationale**: Zustand provides simpler API than Redux while maintaining global state accessibility

The store (`store.js`) manages:
- Nodes and edges arrays
- Node ID generation with type-based counters
- Node/edge change handlers (integrated with ReactFlow)
- Connection handlers for creating edges between nodes
- Field update functionality for node properties

**Pros**: Lightweight, minimal boilerplate, good TypeScript support, easy testing
**Cons**: Less ecosystem/middleware compared to Redux

### Node System

**Problem**: Need extensible system for different node types with varying inputs, outputs, and configuration
**Solution**: BaseNode abstraction with configuration-driven node creation

Each node type is defined by:
- Title and visual styling
- Handles (connection points) with positions and IDs
- Fields (configurable properties like text inputs, selects, textareas)
- Dimensions and custom content

The system supports:
- Target handles (inputs) and source handles (outputs)
- Multiple handles per node at different positions (including top/bottom for complex flows)
- Dynamic field values with default value functions that receive (id, data) parameters
- Custom styling per node type (gradients, colors, borders, rounded corners)
- Field types: text input, number input, select dropdown, textarea
- Static content via children prop for nodes without editable fields

**Node Examples**:
- **Calculator**: Multi-input node with gradient styling and operation selection
- **Filter**: Conditional routing with textarea for condition entry and dual outputs
- **Delay**: Time-based processing with numeric input and unit selection
- **Transformer**: 4-directional handles (top/bottom/left/right) for complex data flow
- **Router**: Multi-output routing with 4 distinct output paths

## External Dependencies

### Core Libraries

**React (v18.2.0)**: UI framework for component-based architecture
- react-dom for rendering
- react-scripts for build tooling (Create React App)

**ReactFlow (v11.8.3)**: Primary dependency for node-graph visualization
- Provides drag-and-drop canvas
- Handle connection management
- Built-in controls (zoom, pan)
- MiniMap and Background components
- Edge types (smoothstep with animated arrows)

**Zustand**: Lightweight state management (imported via `create` from "zustand")
- shallow comparison utility for optimized re-renders

### Development & Testing

- @testing-library/react, @testing-library/jest-dom, @testing-library/user-event for component testing
- web-vitals for performance monitoring

### Build Configuration

The application is configured for Replit hosting with:
- Custom port (5000)
- Host binding to 0.0.0.0
- Disabled host check for development
- WebSocket configuration for hot reloading

### Styling Approach

**Solution**: Inline styles with minimal CSS
**Rationale**: Simple application without need for complex styling system; inline styles provide component-level control

Only global CSS file (index.css) contains base body styling and font definitions.

# Getting Started with Create React App

This project was bootstrapped with [Create React App](https://github.com/facebook/create-react-app).

## Available Scripts

In the project directory, you can run:

### `npm start`

Runs the app in the development mode.\
Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) to view it in your browser.

The page will reload when you make changes.\
You may also see any lint errors in the console.

### `npm test`

Launches the test runner in the interactive watch mode.\
See the section about [running tests](https://facebook.github.io/create-react-app/docs/running-tests) for more information.

### `npm run build`

Builds the app for production to the `build` folder.\
It correctly bundles React in production mode and optimizes the build for the best performance.

The build is minified and the filenames include the hashes.\
Your app is ready to be deployed!

See the section about [deployment](https://facebook.github.io/create-react-app/docs/deployment) for more information.

### `npm run eject`

**Note: this is a one-way operation. Once you `eject`, you can't go back!**

If you aren't satisfied with the build tool and configuration choices, you can `eject` at any time. This command will remove the single build dependency from your project.

Instead, it will copy all the configuration files and the transitive dependencies (webpack, Babel, ESLint, etc) right into your project so you have full control over them. All of the commands except `eject` will still work, but they will point to the copied scripts so you can tweak them. At this point you're on your own.

You don't have to ever use `eject`. The curated feature set is suitable for small and middle deployments, and you shouldn't feel obligated to use this feature. However we understand that this tool wouldn't be useful if you couldn't customize it when you are ready for it.

## Learn More

You can learn more in the [Create React App documentation](https://facebook.github.io/create-react-app/docs/getting-started).

To learn React, check out the [React documentation](https://reactjs.org/).
